production.note: US model years 2017-2019. Start: GM's March 2016 release for the '2017 Corvette Grand Sport': 'The Corvette Grand Sport coupe and convertible go on sale this summer in the U.S.'; Chevrolet's 2017 brochure lists it (gm-2017-corvette-brochure). End: the 2019 model year price list includes '1YW07 | Corvette Grand Sport Coupe' and '1YW67 | Corvette Grand Sport Conv' (cac-2019-corvette-pricing); the C7 ended with the 2019 model year.

body.note: 'The Corvette Grand Sport coupe and convertible go on sale this summer in the U.S.'

displacementL.note: GM's LT1 specifications: 'Displacement: 6.2L (376 cubic inches)'. No opened GM page prints the cc figure.

aspiration.note: Inferred: no forced induction is mentioned for the LT1.

drivetrain.note: Inferred from GM's description of the front-engine Corvette with a 'Standard electronic limited-slip differential' and wider rear wheels and tires; the release does not use the words 'rear-wheel drive'.

transmission.note: 'Seven-speed manual transmission with active rev match and available eight-speed paddle-shift automatic' (a torque-converter automatic). The 2017 brochure: '7-speed manual with Active Rev Matching and launch control' and '8-speed paddle-shift with automatic mode' (gm-2017-corvette-brochure).

powerHp.note: Quote (Chevrolet 2017 brochure, Grand Sport column): "ENGINE 6.2L LT1 V8 / HORSEPOWER 460 @ 6000 rpm / TORQUE 465 lb.-ft. @ 4600 rpm". GM's March 2016 release: "LT1 V8 engine rated at (343 kW) 460 hp, with dry-sump oiling system and active exhaust" (gm-2017-grand-sport-release). Unlike the Stingray, the Grand Sport has the active exhaust as standard, so 460 hp is its standard rating.

weightLb.note: Coupe, 2017 model year. Quote (Chevrolet 2017 brochure): "CURB WEIGHT 3,428 lbs. (coupe) 3,487 lbs. (convertible)". GM gives one figure per body, not per transmission. Chevrolet's 2018 specification table gives the same: "Curb weight, lbs. (kg)" Grand Sport Coupe "3428 (1555)", Grand Sport Convertible "3487 (1582)" (gm-2018-corvette-specs).
